categories.name: Intent & Demand Coverage
categories.question: Across the commercially meaningful things local customers search for, how broadly is this business visible?

categories.name: Maps & Local Pack Visibility
categories.question: How consistently does the business appear prominently in Google's local-business results throughout the target market?

categories.name: Organic Search Visibility
categories.question: How well does the business appear in ordinary Google search results for commercially relevant local intent?

categories.name: AI & Generative Visibility
categories.question: When prospective customers ask AI systems for local service recommendations, how often and how credibly does the business appear?

categories.name: Competitive Share of Visibility
categories.question: Relative to the actual businesses competing for the same local demand, what share of discovery does the business earn?

categories.name: Authority & Entity Footprint
categories.question: How strongly is the business corroborated across external sources that support discovery and recommendation?

categories.name: Visibility Resilience
categories.question: Is discoverability reasonably diversified, or does it depend on one fragile source of visibility?

checks.title: Core service clusters with any qualified visibility
evidence: Core service clusters with qualified visibility: 66.7%.
checks.recommendedIntervention: Prioritize the service clusters with no qualified visibility. Confirm the business actually sells them before treating the gap as a defect.

checks.title: Demand-weighted non-branded coverage
checks.recommendedIntervention: Rebuild the content and entity strategy around the uncovered demand, starting with the highest-weight clusters. Do not optimize a head term at the expense of every other service.

checks.title: High-commercial-intent coverage
checks.recommendedIntervention: Focus the next content and profile work on the commercial intents that are absent.

checks.title: Emergency or urgent intent coverage
checks.recommendedIntervention: Treat emergency visibility as a service-line decision: either build a credible urgent path or state that the business does not offer one.

checks.title: Service + city intent coverage
checks.recommendedIntervention: Create or improve the location-specific service pages and confirm the market is actually served.

checks.title: Near-me intent coverage
checks.recommendedIntervention: Check proximity, service-area configuration, and the strength of the local entity footprint before adding pages.

checks.title: Problem and symptom intent coverage
checks.recommendedIntervention: Map content to the symptoms the business actually solves. Do not publish generic DIY content that cannot produce a service lead.

checks.title: Demand-weighted Local Pack Top-3 coverage
checks.recommendedIntervention: Investigate relevance, proximity, authority, service-area competition, and profile configuration. Cross-reference GBP Scorecard for profile diagnosis.

checks.title: Local Pack Top-10 coverage
checks.recommendedIntervention: Look for the service and geographic clusters where the business disappears, not just the market average.

checks.title: Local Pack Top-20 coverage
checks.recommendedIntervention: Prioritize complete absence over rank improvement. A missing entity is a different problem from a weak rank.

checks.title: Average visible Local Pack position
checks.recommendedIntervention: Use this as context, not as the primary score. Coverage and geographic consistency are more robust.

checks.title: Google Maps Top-3 coverage
checks.recommendedIntervention: Diagnose Maps separately. Check proximity, category relevance, and geographic coverage before assuming a content problem.

checks.title: Google Maps Top-10 coverage
checks.recommendedIntervention: Compare Maps and Local Pack results. A gap between them is diagnostic, not noise.

checks.title: Geo-grid consistency
evidence: Geo-grid coverage: 53.4% of observed grid points.
checks.recommendedIntervention: Use the grid and quadrant summary to find the areas where the business disappears. Do not average the gap away.

checks.title: Service-specific Maps coverage
evidence: Service clusters with at least 40% Maps Top-10 coverage: 50.0%.
checks.recommendedIntervention: Separate the strong service from the weak service in the report. The fix is usually service-specific, not market-wide.

checks.title: Geographic gap severity
checks.recommendedIntervention: Check whether the weak quadrant is actually served. If it is, investigate proximity and location-page coverage.

checks.title: Local Finder coverage
checks.recommendedIntervention: Treat Local Finder as a separate observation. Do not merge it into the Maps rank.

checks.title: Demand-weighted organic Top-3 coverage
checks.recommendedIntervention: Investigate the pages that rank, the intent match, and the authority gap. Cross-reference Website Scorecard for page quality.

checks.title: Organic Top-10 coverage
checks.recommendedIntervention: Focus on the service clusters with no top-10 presence. Confirm a relevant page exists before recommending content.

checks.title: Organic Top-20 coverage
checks.recommendedIntervention: Prioritize complete absence over marginal rank movement.

checks.title: Demand-weighted ranking coverage
checks.recommendedIntervention: Use coverage bands for the primary diagnosis and rank credit as supporting context.

checks.title: Ranking URL relevance to intent
evidence: Dedicated service and problem pages rank for the core service intents, but near-me, city-modified, and high-ticket rankings sometimes resolve to the home page.
checks.recommendedIntervention: Map each commercial intent to a page that genuinely serves it. Do not score page speed, forms, or UX here; those belong to Website Scorecard.

checks.title: City-modified organic coverage
checks.recommendedIntervention: Check location-page coverage and the market configuration before adding pages.

checks.title: Service-cluster organic coverage
evidence: Service clusters with at least 30% organic Top-10 coverage: 66.7%.
checks.recommendedIntervention: Use the cluster view to decide whether the organic gap is service-specific or market-wide.

checks.title: AI mention coverage
checks.recommendedIntervention: Analyze the prompt intents and surfaces where the business is absent. Distinguish mention from recommendation before prescribing a fix.

checks.title: AI recommendation coverage
checks.recommendedIntervention: Analyze the citation and corroboration ecosystem, not just content. A recommendation usually depends on third-party evidence.

checks.title: AI citation and source coverage
checks.recommendedIntervention: Build citable, source-worthy content and third-party corroboration. Do not claim a citation you cannot observe.

checks.title: Service relevance in AI answers
evidence: Every observed mention is for the service in the prompt; no off-service mention was found in the synthetic AI answers.
checks.recommendedIntervention: If relevance is weak, investigate entity ambiguity and content-to-intent mismatch. Do not treat the mention as a win.

checks.title: Location relevance in AI answers
evidence: Every mention places the business in Example County; no out-of-market recommendation was found.
checks.recommendedIntervention: Clarify the service area and entity location. Cross-reference GBP Scorecard for location configuration.

checks.title: Entity accuracy in AI answers
evidence: The observed AI answers use the correct business name and domain wherever the business appears.
checks.recommendedIntervention: Correct the underlying entity footprint and cross-reference GBP Scorecard identity checks. Do not edit an AI answer directly.

checks.title: Competitive share of AI answers
checks.recommendedIntervention: Compare the sources AI systems cite for the competitors. The gap is usually corroboration, not prompt wording.

checks.title: Prompt-intent coverage
checks.recommendedIntervention: Expand prompt coverage and investigate the intents where the business never appears.

checks.title: AI repeat stability
checks.recommendedIntervention: Increase repeats before drawing a conclusion. Report unstable prompts separately.

checks.title: Validated AI surface breadth
checks.recommendedIntervention: Distinguish consumer/search surfaces from model/API surfaces in the report. Do not treat them as equivalent.

checks.title: Business-competitor share of Top-3
checks.recommendedIntervention: Identify the competitors winning the appearances and the surfaces where they win. Do not count directories as contractors.

checks.title: Business-competitor share of Top-10
checks.recommendedIntervention: Compare service by service. A market-wide average can hide a single-service collapse.

checks.title: Maps share of visibility
checks.recommendedIntervention: If Maps share is weak, investigate proximity and local relevance before content.

checks.title: Organic share of visibility
checks.recommendedIntervention: If organic share is weak, investigate page-to-intent coverage and authority.

checks.title: AI recommendation share
checks.recommendedIntervention: Compare the cited sources. AI recommendations often follow corroboration, not direct optimization.

checks.title: Service-specific competitor gap
evidence: Service clusters meeting the competitor median: 33.3%.
checks.recommendedIntervention: Prioritize the clusters where the gap is largest and the service matters commercially.

checks.title: Geographic competitor gap
evidence: Grid quadrants meeting the competitor median: 0.0%.
checks.recommendedIntervention: Use the quadrant comparison to decide whether the gap is geographic or service-specific.

checks.title: Relevant referring domains
checks.recommendedIntervention: Pursue a small number of genuinely relevant local, manufacturer, trade, or association sources. Do not buy generic directory links.

checks.title: Local source relevance
evidence: One local news source and one chamber listing corroborate the business. The remaining local-looking results are generic directories, not independent local corroboration.
checks.recommendedIntervention: Build relationships with local organizations, publications, and trade sources. Do not treat a generic directory as local proof.

checks.title: Industry, manufacturer, and trade sources
checks.recommendedIntervention: Pursue manufacturer/dealer listings, trade associations, and credible trade publications where the business qualifies.

checks.title: External listing and entity consistency
checks.recommendedIntervention: Correct the highest-authority inconsistent listings first. Cross-reference GBP Scorecard for the primary profile.

checks.title: Competitor authority gap
evidence: Relevant domains vs cohort median: 7 vs 9.
checks.recommendedIntervention: Compare the sources the leading competitors have that the business does not. Prioritize relevance over volume.

checks.title: Authority overlap with AI citations
checks.recommendedIntervention: Prioritize sources that both corroborate the entity and appear in AI citations.

checks.title: Surface concentration
checks.recommendedIntervention: Do not weaken a strong surface. Build a second surface as insurance and report the concentration explicitly.

checks.title: Service concentration
checks.recommendedIntervention: Decide whether the concentration is intentional. If not, build visibility for the next most important service.

checks.title: Geographic concentration
checks.recommendedIntervention: Check whether the concentration matches the service area. If not, investigate proximity and location coverage.

checks.title: Branded versus non-branded dependence
checks.recommendedIntervention: Separate branded from non-branded demand in every report. Do not let branded rank inflate the core score.

checks.title: Reproducible visibility trend
checks.recommendedIntervention: Investigate lost visibility by surface and service. Do not invent a trend when the prior run is not comparable.

ownerDataRequired.title: Search Console clicks by query cluster
ownerDataRequired.whyItMatters: Public SERP observation shows where the business appears; Search Console shows whether those impressions produced clicks.
questions: How many non-branded clicks did the tracked service and city query clusters receive in the last 90 days?
Which clusters receive impressions but almost no clicks?

ownerDataRequired.title: Search Console CTR and average position
ownerDataRequired.whyItMatters: A ranking can be visible and still be ignored. CTR and position separate a ranking problem from a result-quality problem.
questions: What are the impressions, clicks, CTR, and average position for each core service cluster?
Does the business appear for the query but lose the click to a directory or a competitor?

ownerDataRequired.title: Priority services by gross profit
ownerDataRequired.whyItMatters: The audit measures visibility across the configured services. The owner knows which services deserve disproportionate attention.
questions: Which service lines produce the highest gross profit per job?
Which services should the business grow, maintain, or stop selling?

ownerDataRequired.title: Qualified leads from non-branded organic search
ownerDataRequired.whyItMatters: Visibility is not the same as qualified demand. Only the owner can show whether an organic visit became a real lead.
questions: How many qualified leads came from non-branded organic search last quarter?

ownerDataRequired.title: Revenue from organic discovery
ownerDataRequired.whyItMatters: A visibility gap matters more when the affected service produces meaningful revenue.
questions: What revenue is attributable to non-branded organic search?
Which service clusters produce the most revenue per organic lead?

ownerDataRequired.title: AI referral traffic
ownerDataRequired.whyItMatters: A mention in an AI answer may or may not produce a visit. Referral data is the only public-adjacent way to see the handoff.
questions: Does analytics show referrals from AI surfaces such as Google AI Mode, ChatGPT, Gemini, Perplexity, or Claude?
Which prompts or landing pages are associated with those referrals?

ownerDataRequired.title: AI-origin leads and jobs
ownerDataRequired.whyItMatters: Being recommended by an AI system is not proof that the recommendation becomes a customer.
questions: Have AI referrals produced qualified leads or booked jobs?
Do customers mention an AI answer when they call or submit a request?

ownerDataRequired.title: Revenue concentration by service and area
ownerDataRequired.whyItMatters: A diversified visibility profile only matters if the underlying revenue is also diversified.
questions: What share of revenue comes from the top service and the top geographic area?
Which service or area would hurt most if visibility declined?

ownerDataRequired.title: Paid discovery return
ownerDataRequired.whyItMatters: Paid search and Local Services Ads are optional discovery channels. Their absence never lowers the public score.
questions: What is the cost per qualified lead for Search Ads and Local Services Ads?
Does paid search cover demand the business cannot earn organically?

journey.label: Search
journey.customerQuestion: When a local customer searches for the service, does the business appear across the demand it sells?

journey.label: Discover
journey.customerQuestion: Does the business appear in Maps, the Local Pack, and ordinary organic results throughout the market?

journey.label: Ask
journey.customerQuestion: When a customer asks an AI system for a recommendation, is the business mentioned, recommended, and cited?

journey.label: Compare
journey.customerQuestion: How does the business's share of discovery compare with real local competitors and credible external sources?

journey.label: Resilience
journey.customerQuestion: Would the business still be discoverable if one surface, service, or area weakened?

journey.label: Handoff
journey.customerQuestion: When the customer chooses the business, do the Google Business Profile and owned website create trust and convert?

journey.label: Measure
journey.customerQuestion: Can discovery-origin demand be tied to qualified leads, jobs, and revenue?

coverage.name: Core service clusters with any qualified visibility

opportunities.label: Paid search coverage
opportunities.why: Paid search can cover high-intent demand that organic and Maps visibility do not reach, but its absence is never a score penalty.
opportunities.evidence: Only recommend when core non-branded coverage is weak and the owner has a paid-media budget.

opportunities.label: Local Services Ads
opportunities.why: Local Services Ads can place a home-service business above the Local Pack for urgent demand.
opportunities.evidence: Only recommend when the trade and market support LSA and the business can answer leads.

opportunities.label: Bing and secondary search coverage
opportunities.why: Secondary engines can be a low-cost incremental discovery surface for some local trades.
opportunities.evidence: Only recommend when the audit shows a measurable gap and the owner wants incremental reach.

opportunities.label: Apple Maps presence
opportunities.why: iPhone users may discover a local business outside Google.
opportunities.evidence: Only recommend when the business has no verified Apple Maps listing.

opportunities.label: Bing Maps presence
opportunities.why: Bing Maps and Bing local results can corroborate the same entity.
opportunities.evidence: Only recommend when the entity footprint is thin or inconsistent.

opportunities.label: Nextdoor and neighborhood presence
opportunities.why: Neighborhood recommendations can matter for service-area businesses.
opportunities.evidence: Only recommend when local corroboration is weak and the market is neighborhood-driven.

opportunities.label: Yelp and marketplace profile
opportunities.why: Some markets and trades see meaningful discovery through marketplaces even when they are not the primary surface.
opportunities.evidence: Only recommend when the marketplace is a real SERP occupier for the tracked services.

opportunities.label: YouTube and video discovery
opportunities.why: Video can occupy SERP features and corroborate the work a business claims to do.
opportunities.evidence: Only recommend when video already appears in the tracked commercial SERPs.

opportunities.label: Local sponsorship and community presence
opportunities.why: Local sponsorships can create relevant local citations and entity corroboration.
opportunities.evidence: Only recommend when local authority is thin and the business is active in the community.

opportunities.label: Manufacturer or dealer directory
opportunities.why: A relevant manufacturer or dealer listing can be a strong, trade-specific corroborating source.
opportunities.evidence: Only recommend when the business sells a manufacturer-backed product or service.

opportunities.label: Local media and PR
opportunities.why: Credible local publications can strengthen the entity footprint and AI citation ecosystem.
opportunities.evidence: Only recommend when the business has a genuine story and local sources are absent.

opportunities.label: AI citation-source development
opportunities.why: AI answers cite sources. Relevant, citable content and third-party corroboration can improve the chance of being referenced.
opportunities.evidence: Only recommend when the business is mentioned but rarely cited, or absent from the sources AI systems use.

opportunities.label: New service-area market
opportunities.why: The audit may reveal a geographic visibility gap that is better addressed by a deliberate market decision than by more content.
opportunities.evidence: Only recommend when the grid shows a durable gap and the owner wants to expand.

opportunities.label: Service and location content expansion
opportunities.why: Organic and AI visibility can be limited by the absence of pages that match the tracked intent.
opportunities.evidence: Only recommend when the ranking URL is missing or generic for a commercially important cluster.

caps.label: No qualified non-branded discovery
caps.rationale: If the business has zero qualified presence across every required core non-branded discovery surface, despite sufficient valid evidence, it cannot be discovered for the demand it sells. The score is capped in the Critical band. This is the only V1 cap.
